title: AI Hub website evaluation
method: Expert review of the live directory (all hubs) using a 1–5 Likert scale. Each dimension is the mean of the criteria below. Freshness and Return-visit pull were added to show what would make people come back more often. Supporting automated checks are in the usability suite run on this page.

dimensions.label: Usefulness
dimensions.summary: The directory gets someone to the right chat UI, coding harness, eval toolkit, or free vendor course quickly. Depth is uneven: Chatbot, Harness, and Evaluation hubs are dense; Courses Hub is a short list with copy errors.

criteria.name: Helps find eval and benchmark tools

evidence: Fourteen hubs cover chat, prompts, harnesses, agents, local models, data, benchmarks, evaluation, security, governance, deployment, and courses.
Evaluation Hub lists Ragas, TruLens, DeepEval, Giskard plus RAG/agent/safety evals.
Prompt and Evaluation concept cards route to ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Claude instead of teaching on the page.
Courses Hub has typos ("providew", "there tooling") and little beyond a vendor URL list.

dimensions.label: Usability
dimensions.summary: Shared dark theme, grouped navigation, and card grids are easy to scan. Automated checks passed 131/131. Remaining friction: dense nav, cards that look clickable but are not links, and thin Courses copy.
evidence: Canonical directory in js/hub.js now includes Evaluation, Courses, and this Site Admin page on every hub.
Automated usability suite: 131 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings (titles, lang, viewport, CSS/JS, alt text, HTTPS).
.card { cursor: pointer } is applied to non-link concept cards, so they look clickable when only the LLM icons act.
No site search; fourteen destinations compete in the top nav.

dimensions.label: Value
dimensions.summary: Free, no account, and current as of September 2026 frontier models. It replaces a pile of bookmarks. Highest value is the Chatbot/Harness snapshot and the Evaluation directory; Courses adds less unique value.

criteria.name: Time saved vs hunting vendor sites

evidence: Chatbot Hub lists Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Grok 4.6, Muse Spark 1.3, and Kimi K3.
Harness Hub lists Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity, OpenCode, Cursor, and Kiro.
Static GitHub Pages hosting: no login, no paywall.
Most concept pages are indexes plus outbound links rather than original tutorials.

dimensions.label: Ease of use
dimensions.summary: First useful click is fast: open a hub, tap a card, land on the vendor. Evaluation is one hop from any page. Remaining ease issues are nav length and mixed card behavior.
evidence: No authentication or onboarding; pages are static HTML.
Evaluation Hub is in AI Data & Evaluation on every page; this report is under Site Admin.
Nav groups wrap into a tall stack on narrower viewports, pushing page content down.
LLM icon buttons are small but labeled with title tooltips.

dimensions.label: Freshness
dimensions.summary: People come back when the catalog changes. Chatbot and Harness hubs are labeled September 2026, but there is no What's New strip, changelog, or last-updated date on most pages — so a repeat visitor cannot tell what is new.
evidence: Chatbot, Harness, and Local Models hubs advertise a September 2026 lineup; Courses and Evaluation do not show a review date.
No homepage changelog, RSS feed, or "updated this week" list.
The site did get a real refresh on 6 Sep 2026 (frontier models + Site Evaluation), which is the kind of change that earns a return visit — it just is not surfaced as news.
To raise this score: add a dated What's New block on the Chatbot Hub and stamp every hub with last reviewed.

dimensions.label: Return-visit pull
dimensions.summary: The hub is a strong launcher, then it sends people away. There is no in-site habit loop (favorites, recents, alerts, weekly roundup), so frequency depends on someone remembering the URL.
evidence: Each hub has a stable URL (index.html, evaluation-hub.html, course-hub.html) that is easy to bookmark or share.
Most cards open a vendor in a new tab, so the session ends on ChatGPT, Claude, or a course site.
No search, no saved-tools list, no email/RSS, no "continue where you left off".
To raise this score: keep a rotating What's New on the homepage, and add a short in-page note on each new model so the hub itself is worth a weekly check.
